name: Deploy
description: Authority to make an already-built version live. Successor to deploy@0.6, which gated 'build and deploy this commit'; this gates the act of putting something in front of real users, because building is not consequential and going live is. The action is a RELEASE: it activates bytes that already exist, so the human can look at the artifact before approving and no rebuild can diverge from what was approved. Host-agnostic — the artifact identifier is a Vercel deployment id, a container image digest, an Azure slot — named by the connector manifest, never here.

release_daily_max.displayName: Times per day something may go live
release_daily_max.description: How often the agent may make a build live for real users. Counted by the Authority Server, so a compromised gateway cannot exceed it. Building a preview is NOT counted: previews harm nobody, and charging them against this limit would exhaust it before anything reached anyone.

rollback_allowed.displayName: May put a previous version back live
rollback_allowed.description: Whether the agent may promote a PREVIOUS artifact back to live. Reverting carries different risk from releasing: the artifact being restored was approved for a moment that has passed. NOT CURRENTLY ENFORCED: no executor yet distinguishes a revert from a release — a rollback arrives as a release of older bytes and is counted by release_daily_max. Hidden from the authorization editor until an executor emits action_type "rollback" for it; kept in the schema so the distinction stays declared.

allowed_repos.description: Repositories the agent may deploy from, e.g. humanagencyprotocol/hap

allowed_environments.description: Deployment targets the agent may reach. Deliberately NOT an enum: hosts disagree — GitHub uses names you define, Vercel has production and preview, Netlify has deploy-preview and branch-deploy. The connector discovers the real list.

allowed_workflows.description: Named pipelines the agent may run, e.g. deploy.yml. Scoping by pipeline rather than by 'deploy' means adding CI later — a migration, an infrastructure apply — is an edit to this list, not a new profile. The limit of this approach: the grant knows a pipeline is permitted, not what it does. The name has to carry that meaning to the human signing.

allowed_branches.description: Branches a deployable commit may come from. Optional: a host with no branch concept leaves it empty.

action_type.description: release or rollback — declared by the manifest, never taken from an agent argument

allowed_repos.description: Repository this action targets, checked against the authorized set

allowed_environments.description: Environment this action targets, checked against the authorized set. Recorded in the receipt, so the proof names where the release went.

allowed_workflows.description: Pipeline this action runs, checked against the authorized set. Recorded in the receipt, so the proof names what ran.

whatsNew: Binds the source commit the build came from, not only the artifact address. A released page can show its commit but never its own deployment URL, so this is what lets a reader tie the page they are on to the approval that put it there.
